events.title: Macintosh 128K released
events.summary: Apple shipped the Macintosh 128K on January 24, 1984 — the first mass-market computer with a graphical user interface and mouse.
events.about: The Mac brought windows, menus, and icons to consumers — HyperCard, MacPaint, and desktop publishing followed. Developers used MPW, Think C, and later CodeWarrior; the GUI forced new interaction models that Windows copied. Susan Kare's icons and the "1984" launch defined how non-programmers could use computers.

narrative.whyChosen: The Macintosh made the GUI a consumer product, not a lab demo.
narrative.whyImportant: It shifted software design toward visual, direct-manipulation interfaces — still the model for web and mobile UI.
narrative.problemSolved: Command-line PCs intimidated mainstream users; Apple bet on approachable graphics and a unified design language.
